extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders in H-1B rulemaking (employers, universities, international students, immigration practitioners, and public commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule preamble responding to public comments about a DHS rule implementing a wage-level weighted H-1B cap selection process, addressing impacts on F-1/OPT students, mid-level workers, STEM fields, academic institutions, and research employers. Provides legal/operational clarifications, empirical rebuttals, and policy rationales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the H-1B program
rubrics_metrics.description: The H-1B program was created to help U.S. employers fill labor shortages in positions requiring highly skilled or highly educated workers while protecting the wages, working conditions, and job opportunities of U.S. workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the policy standard for evaluating whether the rule's outcomes are consistent with congressional/administrative goals; invoked to justify prioritizing higher-skilled/higher-paid beneficiaries over treating the program as an early-career transition pathway for foreign students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection based on highest wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: The weighted selection process generally weights registrations (or petitions, if applicable) based on the highest wage level that the proffered wage will equal or exceed (if OEWS wage level data is available for that occupation and area of employment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational rule for lottery weighting; example explained where F-1 students who earn relatively high salaries may be ranked at higher wage levels (the wage level their proffered wage equals or exceeds) and therefore not be constrained to the lowest wage levels for registration purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain opportunity for H-1B at all wage levels
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule preserves the opportunity for employers to secure H-1B workers at all wage levels, and does not create a barrier to being selected in the H-1B lottery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to rebut claims that the rule would 'determine' access by wage level; repeatedly asserted as a design constraint of the weighted selection mechanism that level I (and other) registrations remain possible selections under the new weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: No impact on OPT or ability to study in the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule has no impact on OPT. It will not impact the ability of international students to study in the United States, which is the basis of their admission to the United States in student status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited to counter assertions that students would be forced to leave or that the rule would block OPT-to-H-1B transitions; DHS emphasizes OPT and study eligibility remain unchanged by the selection-weighting change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule's objective: incentivize higher wages and higher-skilled petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The weighted selection process is designed to incentivize employers to offer higher wages, which generally correlate with higher skill levels, and to petition for positions requiring higher skills and higher-skilled aliens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy rationale: increased chance of selection for higher-wage offers should encourage employers to raise wages or seek higher-skilled roles; framed as balancing employer needs and U.S. worker protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B is not intended as an early-career transition program for foreign students
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the H-1B visa program is not to serve as an early career transition program for foreign students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoked to justify deprioritizing very low-wage/entry-level uses of H-1B and to support the policy goal of reserving the program for higher-skilled hires; used to argue employers should instead recruit American graduates for entry-level roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection is weighted but not determinative based solely on wage levels
rubrics_metrics.description: This final weighted selection process will maintain the opportunity for employers to secure H-1B workers at all wage levels and thus does not 'determine' access to H-1B by wage levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to commenter-cited surveys that mischaracterize the rule as making H-1B 'out of reach' unless compensated at highest levels; DHS stresses distinction between weighting (increasing probability) and determinative exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap exemptions for institutions of higher education and certain nonprofits/research organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1B petitions for aliens who are employed by, or have received offers of employment at, U.S. institutions of higher education, nonprofit entities related to or affiliated with U.S. institutions of higher education, or nonprofit research organizations or governmental research organizations are exempt from the H-1B cap (INA sec. 214(g)(5), 8 U.S.C. 1184(g)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a legal limitation on the rule’s effect; DHS cites FY2025 approval counts showing many research and academic petitions are cap-exempt and therefore unaffected by the weighted cap-selection change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projected selection probability effects by wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS projects that under the weighted selection process level II and level III groups will have an increased probability of selection compared to the current random selection process, with the probability of selection increasing by 3 percent for level II and by 55 percent for level III (as noted in Table 13 of the NPRM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative metric DHS uses to argue the rule benefits mid-level and higher-wage beneficiaries and does not unduly disadvantage certain wage categories; forms part of DHS’s empirical rebuttal to commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for claims of harm (surveys & causal linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS requires credible evidence and causal linkage to conclude the rule will cause harms like declines in international student enrollment or cascading economic effects; DHS reviewed cited surveys and found the survey questions inaccurate or not dispositive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS dismisses commenter claims unsupported by direct evidence connecting the weighted-selection change to declines in enrollment or local economic collapse; emphasizes the need for appropriately phrased survey questions and relevant data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule facilitates admission and retention of higher-skilled foreign workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitating the admission of higher-skilled foreign workers, as indicated by their earning of wages that equal or exceed higher prevailing wage levels, is expected to increase the United States’ competitive edge in attracting the 'best and the brightest' and benefit the economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy claim used to rebut arguments that the rule will deter top students; DHS asserts higher-paid foreign graduates will see increased lottery selection probability under weighted selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve research and academic workforce via cap exemptions and weighting benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Many employers and aliens described by commenters (universities, nonprofit research organizations, governmental research organizations) would be cap-exempt and therefore not impacted by this rule; where researchers are cap-subject, the rule increases chance of selection for highly paid, highly skilled foreign researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to rebut claims that research, universities, and grant deliverables will be harmed; DHS cites cap-exempt approval counts (FY2025) to show scale of unaffected petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterfactual hiring guidance for employers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a U.S. company wishes to focus its talent acquisition policies on hiring recent graduates, it may focus its search among American graduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical policy suggestion and normative standard: employers seeking entry-level talent should consider domestic hiring rather than relying on H-1B for early-career positions; used to support the rule’s aim to protect U.S. entry-level opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level I registrations remain selectable; rule does not eliminate low-wage positions
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS disagrees with the concern that level I positions will be eliminated by this rule. The weighted selection implemented through this rule favors allocation to higher-paid and higher-skilled aliens while maintaining the opportunity for employers to secure H-1B workers at all wage levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that although probability is shifted, the mechanism is not a categorical ban on low-wage selections; used to rebut claims of absolute exclusion and predicted complete elimination of entry-level roles.
